taxonomic_note: Keep separate accepted Agave univittata; only its historical var. tamaulipasana is listed here as a synonym.
look_here_first: Look at narrow rigid rosette leaves, their spaced marginal teeth, and the terminal spine; then inspect the largely spike-like flowering axis. Distinguish A. univittata with leaf-edge detail, not size alone.

best_field_traits: Leaf teeth about 2–6 mm, mostly spaced 2–4 cm apart; terminal spine 1.5–4.5 cm.
Flowering axis largely spike-like, about 2–3.5 m in the existing FNA-based review.
morphology_keys.leaves: Rigid narrow leaves in a basal rosette; inspect edge teeth and terminal spine with scale.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Tall largely spicate flowering axis; habit and axis are visible in the USDA photograph, but individual flowers are not resolved.
morphology_keys.lookalike_separators: A. americana has much broader leaves and a branched panicle. A. univittata has undulate/crenate, less detachable leaf margins and teeth mostly 1–2 cm apart; overlaps require close leaf-edge and flowering evidence. Hybridization is documented in FNA; avoid size-only identification.

source_pool_review.taxonomy_review: Reviewed 2026-10-09 — accepted Agave lechuguilla Torr. (POWO/WCVP); Texas native at STATE level (Chihuahuan Desert), target-zone three-county status UNRESOLVED. Preserve learner approval, no native PASS. Historic Agave univittata var. tamaulipasana belongs under A. lechuguilla in POWO; do not merge accepted A. univittata species. Sources: https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:60474750-2 ; https://efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242101309
source_pool_review.curation_status_before_install: Taxonomy reviewed — approved_pending_curation; range UNRESOLVED; not canonical
source_pool_review.diagnostic_notes: LOOK HERE FIRST: narrow erect 30–50 × 2–4(-5.2) cm rigid leaves with teeth 2–6 mm mostly 2–4 cm apart, apical spine 1.5–4.5 cm; flowering axis largely spike-like (2–3.5 m) vs branched A. americana panicle. Similar A. univittata has undulate/crenate, less detachable leaf margins and teeth mostly 1–2 cm apart; overlap demands flowers/leaf-edge close-up. FNA notes hybridization with other agaves; don't use size alone. PHOTO ROLES: leaf cross-profile + margins with scale, spine, full flowering axis, paired A. univittata edge.
source_pool_review.accepted_name_note: Accepted Agave lechuguilla Torr.; synonyms include Agave poselgeri Salm-Dyck and Agave univittata var. tamaulipasana (A.Berger) Jacobson. A. univittata is a separate accepted species.
